reviews.body:
Thanks for tackling the OpenAI default migration and updating the related docs. I have a few suggestions on test coverage, the smoke-test configuration, release notes, and the PR description; none are merge blockers.

4 approved findings: 3 inline, 1 in this review body.

### General

**RECOMMENDED** The PR description covers `OpenAIChatConfig`, Spring Boot `OpenAIProperties`, a `gpt-3.5-turbo` migration, Java tests, and Maven commands. This change updates Python provider defaults from `gpt-5-mini`, so the description misstates both the implementation and how it was tested.

Please update it to describe the `OpenAIProvider` and shared agent-builder default changes, the documentation updates, and the Python test commands and results. Remove the unrelated Java and Maven claims.

<!-- conductor-review:v2: -->

review_comments.body:
**RECOMMENDED** The updated test checks the provider's constructor state, but it doesn't verify the request sent when execution uses the default model. The HTTP-stub tests explicitly choose `gpt-5-mini`, and the execution tests mock the builder, so they don't cover that path either.

Please add a hermetic `httpx.MockTransport` test using the real provider and builder without model overrides. Check that the request uses `gpt-5.6-terra`, ordinary execution omits an unset output cap, and dialog requests still send `max_completion_tokens=4096`.

**RECOMMENDED** `tests/test_integration/test_openai_real_api.py` still defaults `CONDUCTOR_TEST_OPENAI_MODEL` to `gpt-5-mini` and passes it to both agents. That means these opt-in tests bypass the new provider default and will keep requesting the retiring model after December 11.

Let `None` reach the provider when no override is set, while keeping custom model overrides supported:

```suggestion
_TEST_MODEL = os.getenv("CONDUCTOR_TEST_OPENAI_MODEL")
```

**RECOMMENDED** Workflows using the implicit default will see a pricing change as soon as they upgrade, not just when `gpt-5-mini` retires. OpenAI lists standard input/output rates of $0.25/$2 per million tokens for GPT-5 Mini and $2/$12 for Terra: 8× the input price and 6× the output price. The release note mentions the availability fix but not this budget impact.

Please add a migration note for users relying on the implicit default:

```suggestion
If you rely on the implicit model default, review your budget or select a model explicitly. See the [GPT-5.6 Terra pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra).
```
